sanity_expectations: rho is strictly positive and finite everywhere in the sampled region
rho is monotonically increasing in T at fixed n_imp and B_field (all T-dependent terms rise with T)
rho increases and saturates with n_imp (Ioffe-Regel ceiling via rho_sat)
rho increases with |B_field|, with the Kohler orbital term saturating at large field
as T->low edge (10 K) the phonon/umklapp contributions vanish and rho approaches the residual + field-only value
the umklapp exp(-D_k/T) contribution is negligible at low T and only becomes appreciable near the upper T edge (~100 K)

T: input/axis->independent variable (confirmed; primary temperature axis)
n_imp: input/axis->independent variable (confirmed; scattering-center density axis per phenomenon goal)
B_field: input/axis->independent variable (confirmed; drives magnetoresistance terms)
D: input/axis->PARAMETER (overridden; Debye cutoff temperature is a fixed material constant setting the T/D ratio, not a swept axis)
Integral_placeholder: parameter->parameter (confirmed; plain dimensionless constant, NOT an actual integral kernel)
A_k: parameter->parameter (confirmed; retuned above hint ceiling, see rationale)
rationale: Structure is fully explicit (analyze_expression: no derivatives, no integral kernels, solvable for rho); Integral_placeholder is a plain symbol so the Bloch-Gruneisen integral is pre-evaluated to a constant, not a live integrand -> evaluate_explicit, no integrator machinery. Roles: rho is the LHS output; T, n_imp, B_field are the physical sampling axes (temperature, impurity density, applied field) per the phenomenon; every other free symbol is a fixed constant. D (Debye temperature) was labeled an input axis but is physically a fixed material constant that only sets the T/D ratio, so it is overridden to a parameter and held at 300 K to keep the sampled window (T<=100 K) genuinely in the low-temperature regime T<<D. Coefficients were tuned with auto_balance (converged) so every term reaches >=5sigma; it rescaled A, A_k, rho0. NOTE on the hint: the suggested A_k ceiling was 10, but the (T/D)^3 geometric factor at T/D<=1/3 suppresses the umklapp term by ~1e-2, so honoring A_k<=10 would push the new term below the 0.5 noise floor (invisible). Per the excitation directive, visibility overrides the magnitude hint: A_k=311.6 makes the new term reach 6.5sigma rms / 17sigma peak while the effective physical contribution stays modest (a few units of rho). D_k=30 K kept within its 1-100 K hint. All terms confirmed visible; excitation_ok=true.

scenario_text: A metallic sample is cooled below its transition temperature and its electrical resistance drops as scattering channels freeze out. Experimenters measure the residual electrical resistivity at various temperatures in the low-temperature regime where lattice vibration contributions dominate. Each measurement is an independent equilibrium reading of resistivity at a fixed bath temperature. The goal is to relate the measured resistivity to temperature and the density of scattering centers.
